newsitem.title: UK: London stocks end firm as Wall St rally continues.
newsitem.headline: London stocks end firm as Wall St rally continues.

text.p: UK shares closed higher for the second day running, lifted by Wall Street's recent strength as well as continued bid speculation.
Dealers believe the FTSE could test its all-time highs in the next few days, provided Wall Street maintains its current upward momentum.
"This is all about the Dow. It's had a pretty rough time the past few weeks but seems to be bouncing back," one senior dealer said.
"We're(UK share market)are just along for the ride."
The FTSE 100 ended 33.1 points higher at 4,051.3.
The Dow industrials, which has risen over 70 points the previous two sessions, jumped 50 points in the opening minutes of trade on Thursday, and was up 46.9 points at 6,393.67 by 1630 GMT.
FTSE trading volume was in excess of 950 million shares, the highest level since April.
"The better volume is encouraging. At the beginning of the weak it looked as though the market was winding down for Christmas," another dealer said.
"But, if volumes remain high we may yet get our traditional end of year rally."
The FTSE is only 21.8 points away from its all-time closing peak of 4,073.1, set on October 21.
Technical analysts believe that barrier could fall by year end but expect the FTSE to meet fierce resistance at the 4,100-4,010 level.

"I don't see much scope for the FTSE to go much beyond 4,100," said Kirit Shah, analyst at Sanwa International. I expect the FTSE to remain trapped in a range of 3,900-4,100 for the near-term at least."
Shah also doubts the Dow's recent rally will last although he doesn't rule out further near-term strength.
GKN nosedived 35-1/2p, or three percent, to 10.09-1/2 stg after a U.S. court ordered the UK auto component group to pay its franchisees $398 million in damages.
The company also said the damages could be increased to $554 million but said it would try to have the verdict overturned or damages reduced.
Amongst second-line stocks, United News & Media jumped 23-1/2p at 683-1/2p after analysts at SBC Warburg reiterated a "buy" recommendation.
Laporte also benefited from a "buy" note, gaining 26-1/2p at 661p.
"The technical picture for the Dow is looking a bit better than it did a few days ago. We could see it bounce a bit more," Shah said.
"But I wouldn't get too carried away. It is still overbought and still subject to more downside pressure.
For Friday, the FTSE's first resistance point is around the all-time closing high of 3,073. The next target is 4,100, technical analysts said.
Continued bid speculation in several sectors, including banking, insurance, and pharmaceuticals also added to the FTSE's new-found confidence.
Abbey National briefly touched an all-time trading high of 750p, before closing at 743p, up 6-1/2p as the rumour mill pointed to the banking group as a bid or merger candidate.
Storehouse was also cited as a bid target although its 8-1/2p rise at 261p was attributed to its 8.4 million share placement during the session which was well received by the market, dealers said.
B.A.T Industries, which some people believe could be in the market to take over a UK insurance company, gained 20p at 486-1/2p, helped by the recent strong showing by tobacco stocks in the U.S.
--Dale Faulken, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
